title: NLTI Gate 7 — Routing, Model, RAG and Write Safety
description: Gate 7 verification dashboard for #1219. Most panels read the nlti.request.telemetry v1 JSON stream from Loki; HTTP-status and preload panels read Prometheus. Fields that the emitter does not populate yet are marked GAP in the panel description. See pos-mcp-server/docs/dashboards/nlti-overview.md.

list.name: role
list.label: Primary role (regex)
list.description: Regex matched against actor.primaryRole. A textbox, not a query variable: actor_primaryRole is a pipeline-parsed label, so Loki's label_values API cannot enumerate it. Default .* matches every role.

panels.title: Routing mix by intent type
panels.description: routing.intentType from the Gate 4 T1 router decision. Empty series = requests with no router decision (Tier-0 simple chat, or the tiered router disabled).

targets.expr: sum by (routing_intentType) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | actor_primaryRole =~ "$role" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Routing mix by domain and risk level
panels.description: routing.domain and routing.riskLevel. riskLevel drives the write-gate policy (WritePlanPolicy: stale-data protection applies to risk >= MEDIUM).

targets.expr: sum by (routing_domain) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | actor_primaryRole =~ "$role" [$__interval]))

sum by (routing_riskLevel) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | actor_primaryRole =~ "$role" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Workflow-state mix and Tier-0 rule hits
panels.description: routing.workflowState is the Gate 2C session workflow (IDLE, CREATING_PO, RECEIVING_ASN, INVENTORY_RECON, PROCESSING_RETURN). routing.simpleChatRule names the Tier-0 rule that short-circuited the router.

targets.expr: sum by (routing_workflowState) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | actor_primaryRole =~ "$role" [$__interval]))

sum by (routing_simpleChatRule) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | routing_simpleChatRule != "" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Requests by serving tier
panels.description: routing.tier: T0_RULE (simple-chat short circuit), T1_ROUTER, T2_SIMPLE, T2_COMPLEX. This is the #1216 routing-mix metric.

targets.expr: sum by (routing_tier) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | actor_primaryRole =~ "$role" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Tier share (dashboard window)
panels.description: Same source as the tier timeseries, aggregated over the selected range. Use this for the Gate 4 / Gate 7 tier-mix evidence table.

targets.expr: sum by (routing_tier) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" [$__range]))

panels.title: Executing model by tier
panels.description: model.tierModel is the model name the tier executor actually used; model.routerModel is the T1 classifier model. An empty tierModel with a non-empty tier means the tier resolved to the default chat model (MCP_MODEL_SIMPLE / MCP_MODEL_COMPLEX unset).

targets.expr: sum by (routing_tier, model_tierModel) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Model fallback rate (model.fallbackUsed)
panels.description: GAP: NltiRequestTelemetryFactory hardcodes Model.fallbackUsed=false and the fallbackChatModel bean (ModelFallbackConfiguration) is never injected into a call path, so this reads 0 by construction. The query is correct against the v1 schema and will populate once failover is wired and the flag is set.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | model_fallbackUsed = "true" [$__range])) / clamp_min(sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" [$__range])), 1)

panels.title: Tier model-resolution fallbacks (WARN)
panels.description: Real fallback signal available today: TieredChatModelResolver logs at WARN when a tier cannot apply its model override and silently serves the default model. Non-zero here invalidates any tier-quality comparison.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server", level="WARN"} |= "MCP tiered model resolver" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Requests served with no tier decision
panels.description: Proxy for 'the tiered router did not run': telemetry events where routing.tier is absent. Expected to be ~0 when MCP_MODEL_TIERING_ENABLED=true; a rising share means requests are bypassing the router.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | routing_tier = "" [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | routing_tier != "" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Prompt-layer composition rate by layer
panels.description: rag.promptLayers is a JSON array, which Loki's bare `| json` skips; each series therefore uses `| json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers"` plus a quoted-token label filter. Layers are BASE, ROLE, DOMAIN, TOOL_USE, WRITE_GATE (NltiRequestTelemetry.PromptLayer). This is the Gate 1 (#1213) evidence panel.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"BASE"` [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"ROLE"` [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"DOMAIN"` [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"TOOL_USE"` [$__interval]))

sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"WRITE_GATE"` [$__interval]))

panels.title: Requests composed with no prompt layers
panels.description: NltiRequestTelemetryFactory omits the whole rag object when RolePromptResolver.assemble() returned no layers (no seeded master prompt or no role persona). Sustained non-zero means prompt seeding is broken for some role.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers = "" [$__interval]))
sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server", level="WARN"} |~ "MCP no master prompt seeded|MCP no role persona seeded" [$__interval]))

panels.title: 403 responses on NLTI / MCP routes
panels.description: Real permission-reject signal today. Covers SessionOwnershipViolationException and the write-gate dual permission check (NltiWritePlanService.requireToolPermission throws AccessDeniedException). Split by templated uri so confirm/cancel denials are distinguishable.

targets.expr: sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service="pos-mcp-server", uri=~"/v1/(mcp|nlt)/.*", status="403"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60
sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service="pos-mcp-server", uri=~"/v1/(mcp|nlt)/.*", status="401"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Caller permission-code count (p05 / p50)
panels.description: actor.permissionCodeCount from telemetry. A p05 collapsing toward 0 means the gateway bitset decode or the role-default permission fetch is failing, which manifests downstream as tool-selection and RAG-visibility rejects.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.05, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap actor_permissionCodeCount [$__interval])

quantile_over_time(0.50, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap actor_permissionCodeCount [$__interval])

panels.title: Tool candidates rejected for permissions (tools.rejectedPermissionCount)
panels.description: GAP: NltiRequestTelemetryFactory hardcodes Tools.rejectedPermissionCount=0. Tool permission gating runs in SQL (ToolMetadataRepository.findEnabledByPermissionsAndWorkflow), so the rejected candidates are never materialized in Java and there is no count to thread through; PermissionAwareMetadataFilter's DEBUG drop count is RAG documents, not tools, and must not be substituted here. The query is correct against the v1 schema and reads 0 until tool selection returns its rejected set — use the 403 panel above meanwhile.

targets.expr: sum_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap tools_rejectedPermissionCount [$__interval])

sum_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | unwrap tools_candidateCount [$__interval])

panels.title: Top retrieved-document score (rag.retrieved)
panels.description: GAP: NltiRequestTelemetryFactory always passes null for Rag.retrieved (Gate 5 has not wired retrieval scores into the emitter), so this panel has no data today. The expression uses Loki's indexed JSON expression syntax because rag.retrieved is an array, which a bare `| json` skips. Use the DOMAIN-layer and preload panels beside it as the interim recall signal, and scripts/rag_lock_sweep.py for corpus-level recall evidence.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.50, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json top_score="rag.retrieved[0].score" | top_score != "" | unwrap top_score [$__interval])

quantile_over_time(0.05, {job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json top_score="rag.retrieved[0].score" | top_score != "" | unwrap top_score [$__interval])

panels.title: DOMAIN prompt-layer rate (RAG-scoped prompt composed)
panels.description: Interim recall signal that is emitted today. The DOMAIN layer is added by RolePromptResolver only when the selected tools resolved a rag-scope, so its share tracks whether requests are being grounded at all. A drop with steady traffic means rag-scope resolution or the preloaded corpus regressed.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json prompt_layers="rag.promptLayers" | prompt_layers =~ `"DOMAIN"` [$__interval])) / clamp_min(sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" [$__interval])), 1)

panels.title: Static RAG corpus preload health
panels.description: Corpus availability underpins recall. mcp.rag.preload.duration is timed once per StaticRagPreloadService run (startup); the WARN stream carries per-document failures. Any preload failure means the 39-doc corpus is incomplete and Gate 5 recall numbers are not comparable.

targets.expr: sum(increase(mcp_rag_preload_duration_seconds_count{service="pos-mcp-server"}[1h]))
sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server", level="WARN"} |= "Preload failed for document_id=" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Write-plan confirm / cancel outcomes by HTTP status
panels.description: Corroborating HTTP view of the write-gate endpoints — kept beside the telemetry outcome panel below rather than as its substitute (#1397). NltiExceptionHandler maps the write-plan failure modes onto distinct statuses: 404 WRITE_PLAN_NOT_FOUND, 409 WRITE_PLAN_CONFLICT / WRITE_PLAN_STALE, 410 WRITE_PLAN_EXPIRED, 403 permission re-check failure, 5xx WRITE_PLAN_EXECUTION_FAILED. It still answers something the outcome panel cannot: a confirm that passed the gate and then failed downstream reports outcome=confirmed with a 5xx here.

targets.expr: sum by (uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service="pos-mcp-server", uri=~"/v1/nlt/requests/\\{requestId\\}/(confirm|cancel)"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60

panels.title: Write-capable requests and plans created
panels.description: write.isWrite is emitted by both paths: by the chat managers when the request's candidate tools included a write-capable tool, and (since #1397) by NltiRequestServiceImpl for every ACTION-classified NLTI submit — the Gate 6 preview trigger. The plan-created series is the INFO log NltiWritePlanService emits after persisting a PENDING_CONFIRMATION plan. A widening gap between them means write intents are being detected but not turned into plans.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | write_isWrite = "true" [$__interval]))
sum(count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "NLTI write plan created" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Confirmation outcome mix (write.confirmationOutcome)
panels.description: Live since #1397: NltiWritePlanService emits an nlti.request.telemetry record carrying write.confirmationOutcome at every terminal confirmation decision (confirmed|cancelled|expired|stale-data|superseded), alongside the nlti_audit_event ledger row. The same outcomes are mirrored onto the nlt_write_plan_confirmation_count_total counter, tagged outcome — use that for alerting, since Prometheus alert rules cannot query Loki. GET /v1/nlt/audit remains the authoritative compliance record.

targets.expr: sum by (write_confirmationOutcome) (count_over_time({job="docker", service="pos-mcp-server"} |= "nlti.request.telemetry" | regexp `(?P<telemetry>[{]"schemaVersion".+[}])` | line_format "{{.telemetry}}" | json | __error__="" | write_confirmationOutcome != "" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Adaptive tuning proposals by mode
panels.description: Supporting panel for the #1219 shadow-to-live tuning verification. mcp.tuning.proposals is tagged with mode (shadow|live) by ToolPriorityTuningService; a live-mode proposal writes mcp_tool.priority.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (increase(mcp_tuning_proposals_total{service="pos-mcp-server"}[1h]))
